Sydney star Charlie Curnow kicked six goals against the Western Bulldogs to take the lead in the Coleman Medal race. (Getty Images Brendon Thorne/AFL Photos)

Charlie Curnow is in the hunt for a third Coleman Medal after booting six goals to fire Sydney to a 35-point win over the Western Bulldogs.

It was deja vu for the Dogs, with Curnow slamming through four first-half goals at the SCG as the Swans outclassed the visitors 13.12 (90) to 7.13 (55).

Curnow had been the Bulldogs' tormentor in round seven, finishing with seven goals in Sydney's 66-point demolition job.

After Friday's haul in front of 35,227 fans, the 29-year-old is the leading goalkicker with 44 goals — ahead of Gold Coast's Ben King (43).

Second-placed Sydney (13-3) returned to winning ways after a dismal 43-point loss to the Brisbane Lions, despite six personnel changes for the club's annual Pride Game.

Swans coach Dean Cox was forced to make four through injury — Joel Amartey (Achilles), Logan McDonald (quad), Pete Ladhams (groin) and Sam Wicks (hamstring).

The eighth-placed Western Bulldogs (9-7) fell short in a finals litmus test and injuries to defenders Connor Budarick (ankle) and Nick Coffield (concussion) only add to their woes.

Budarick was forced out of the game in the second quarter, while a diving Coffield was hit in the back of the head by the knee of Swans midfielder Chad Warner.

The Dogs will also be sweating on the match review officer's verdict of Matthew Kennedy's high bump on Sydney opponent Caiden Cleary.

In Friday night's second match, Adelaide held off a fast-finishing West Coast side to record a 25-point win at Perth Stadium.

Adelaide kicked six goals to one in the opening quarter to take command of the contest, but was forced to defend grimly in the final term to record a 15.9 (99) to 11.8 (74) win.

Izak Rankine and skipper Jordan Dawson finished with a game-high 27 disposals apiece, while Darcy Fogarty kicked four goals in Riley Thilthorpe's absence.

Fri 3 Jul 2026 at 11:19pm

By Chris De Silva

Convincing wins then for both Sydney and Adelaide, who enhance their top-four credentials.

Sydney draws to within four points of Fremantle (56 points), although the Dockers have a game in hand and a superior percentage (148.2).

Adelaide (40 points) draws level with the fourth-placed Brisbane Lions.

We'll be back again tomorrow afternoon for four matches, beginning with a crucial clash between Hawthorn and Melbourne in Launceston.

Please join us again then!

Fri 3 Jul 2026 at 10:55pm

By Chris De Silva

Key Event

Fri 3 Jul 2026 at 10:48pm

By Chris De Silva

Adelaide holds on for a 25-point win over West Coast in a contest that proved to be a lot tougher than we initially thought!

The Crows came out of the gates with a tremendous first quarter, kicking six goals to one, and really that five-goal margin was what held throughout the night.

West Coast, to their credit, gave a good account of themselves in the final three quarters, but that first quarter put them in a hole that was just a little too deep.

Izak Rankine and Jordan Dawson finish the match as the joint-leading ball-winners on the ground with 27 touches a piece, while also combining for 13 clearances.

Harley Reid also enjoyed a strong outing for the Eagles, finishing with 23 touches and six clearances.

A dominant final quarter from West Coast evened up the overall numbers, but Adelaide is well-deserving of this win.

The Crows pick up a crucial four points to stay in touch with the top four on the AFL ladder.

Fri 3 Jul 2026 at 10:42pm

By Chris De Silva

Ben Keays nails his second goal of the final quarter and that'll do it here!

The Crows kicked it out of congestion at halfback and then a horror bounce did for the Eagles defender rushing up to collect the ball.

Adelaide gets out the back, and they show excellent composure to share it around before Keays takes an uncontested mark inside 50.

Just three minutes left now.

Fri 3 Jul 2026 at 10:39pm

By Chris De Silva

Adelaide still clinging to an 18-point lead as we tick into the last five minutes of this one.

West Coast continuing to dominate the territory, but they need goals, not metreage right now.

Fri 3 Jul 2026 at 10:37pm

By Chris De Silva

The Eagles are throwing the kitchen sink at the Crows here!

There's 6:40 left on the clock and they need three goals to tie things up.

The inside 50 count reads 16-3 West Coast's way for the quarter.

Fri 3 Jul 2026 at 10:32pm

By Chris De Silva

West Coast continues to hang around!

Milan Murdock sends a long ball inside 50 towards Jake Waterman, who is outmanned two on one.

Waterman manages to bring the ball to ground level, and then he shrugs off the tackle and manages to get a kick away to Tom Cole, who snaps truly from close range.

Margin back to 18 points with 10:08 left on the clock.

Fri 3 Jul 2026 at 10:30pm

By Chris De Silva

Ben Keays drills a MASSIVE goal against the run of play!

The ball was parked in West Coast's half, and the Crows were finally able to break through the press and they get a goal out of it.

Keays takes a diving mark deep in the pocket and snaps truly on the left foot.

Adelaide leading by 24 points with 11:04 left on the clock. Still enough time for West Coast to pull off the comeback, but that goal makes it tough.

Fri 3 Jul 2026 at 10:26pm

By Chris De Silva

The inside 50 count reads 11-0 West Coast's way in the final term so far.

Suddenly, after dominating most of the match, Adelaide's back six is under immense pressure.

The Eagles can sense they're in with a shot here.

Key Event

Fri 3 Jul 2026 at 10:24pm

By Henry Hanson

It was far from a classic at the SCG, but Sydney fans won't care.

The Swans bounce back from the disappointment of last week with a convincing, professional 35-point win over a lacklustre pack of Bulldogs.

Charlie Curnow the undoubted star for the Swans.

The big man finishes with six goals, becoming the Coleman Medal leader in the process, while Haydne McLean (three goals) was very impressive on his return to the team.

Isaac Heeney (one goal, 27 disposals) was typically influential, conclusively winning his heavyweight midfield bout with the quiet Marcus Bontempelli (19 disposals, two behinds).

For the Bulldogs, it's a bit of a nothing display - but a 35-point loss at the SCG is far from a disaster.

They'll remain confident of securing a finals berth.

Next up for the Swans, a mouthwatering meeting with Fremantle in the west.

Fri 3 Jul 2026 at 10:22pm

By Chris De Silva

THE EAGLES AREN'T DONE YET FOLKS!

Jake Waterman gets on the end of a loose ball after some brilliant forward 50 pressure, and he snaps truly from close range.

Waterman's got three goals for the night now, and the margin is down to three even goals with 17:15 left.

West Coast has the first five clearances of the quarter.

Fri 3 Jul 2026 at 10:20pm

By Henry Hanson

Sydney has kicked another goal at the SCG, with Joel Hamling slotting a rare major.

He's expertly found from deep, marking in the goal square and making no mistake.

Swans leading by 35 points with a couple minutes to play.

Fri 3 Jul 2026 at 10:18pm

By Chris De Silva

The Eagles are showing some signs of life here!

Bo Allan drills a pretty tricky set shot after reciving a good short kick from Jack Graham, and the margin is down to 24 points!

West Coast has nine of the last 10 inside 50s in this match including the first four of the final quarter.

Key Event

Fri 3 Jul 2026 at 10:12pm

By Chris De Silva

So we're back where we were at half-time after both West Coast and Adelaide kick 4.3 to share the spoils in the third quarter.

The Crows looked like they were going to break it open in the early stages, leading by as many as 42 points, but once again the Eagles have stayed in it, juuust.

The clearance discrepancy is still proving tough to overcome for the Eagles despite their overall intensity being quite good.

Adelaide leads the clearance count 32-24 for the match, including a 15-5 lead out of centre bounces.

It's led to a 49-26 smashing in the inside 50 count, and really, given those numbers, the Eagles have to feel pretty good to even be this close.

Izak Rankine and Rory Laird lead all players with 22 touches apiece, with Rankine also adding six clearances and a goal.

Liam Duggan is West Coast's high man with 19 touches, while Jobe Shanahan and Jake Waterman have combined for five goals.

Fri 3 Jul 2026 at 10:11pm

By Henry Hanson

There are nine minutes remaining at the SCG, where an already scrappy game is disintegrating even further.

Regular stoppages and skirmishes really robbing the Bulldogs of any momentum.

Swans by 31.

Fri 3 Jul 2026 at 10:07pm

By Henry Hanson

Charlie Curnow continues his excellent night, marking on the arc and walloping one through the big sticks.

That's half a dozen for big Charlie.

Arty Jones responds with a set shot of his own for the Bulldogs, narrowing the margin to 30 points as we approach the halfway point in the final term.

Fri 3 Jul 2026 at 10:06pm

By Henry Hanson

Stoppages and skirmishes galore in Sydney.

Nick Coffield receives a really concerning but completely unintentional knee to the head in a tussle with Chad Warner.

He's looking a bit groggy and shaken and is rightly off for an HIA.

Fri 3 Jul 2026 at 10:05pm

By Chris De Silva

West Coast aren't going to go quietly into the night!

The Crows get a little too cute looking to come out of 50 and the Eagles are able to force the turnover.

Jobe Shanahan kicks up the loose ball and snaps truly from 20m out for his third goal of the evening.

West Coast trims the margin to 29 points with 2:46 left in the third term.

Fri 3 Jul 2026 at 10:04pm

By Chris De Silva

Jobe Shanahan takes a big contested mark inside 50 and drills the set shot to stem the tide for West Coast.

Shanahan's now kicked 20 goals for the season, second only to Jake Waterman.

He's turning into a terrific key forward prospect for the Eagles!
